open_points.subject: Operator access to instance configuration
open_points.text: “An agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read the store and the instance's configuration, service tokens included” contradicts “An instance's configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and the Registry process.”
open_points.question: Is an operator agent itself authorized to read Registry's configuration and service tokens, or does “the owner's own hand” classify it as the owner for this boundary?
options: The operator agent is treated as the owner and may read all configuration and secrets.
Only the human owner and Registry process may read the configuration; operator access must exclude it.
Operator access depends on the particular tool or deployment and must be stated separately.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the operator agent as the owner for host access and therefore allow it to read the configuration and secrets.

open_points.subject: Operator disclosure to model providers
open_points.text: “Operator — `onboard_object`, or an agent preparing a client message for the owner” is followed by “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model the owner runs it on.”
open_points.question: Does contact data pass to a model provider only when the operator is a model-backed agent, or also whenever the standalone `onboard_object` script is used?
options: Only model-backed agent operations disclose contact data to the model provider.
Every use of `onboard_object` is mediated by a model and discloses the data.
The script and model-backed agent are separate actors with separate disclosure boundaries.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the standalone script and the model-backed agent as separate actors; only the agent discloses contact data to a model provider.

open_points.subject: Personal-data readers
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff only (R0-09)” conflicts with “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model the owner runs it on — today Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for Codex.”
open_points.question: Does “readable by staff only” describe only authorization to Registry's customer-read actions, or does it promise that no non-staff party, including a model provider, receives the data?
options: It is only an API authorization rule; an operator's model provider is an accepted external recipient.
It is an end-to-end confidentiality promise, so contact data cannot be sent to a model provider.
Model providers are deemed part of the staff trust domain for this purpose.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as an API authorization rule with model providers as an explicitly accepted external disclosure.
